## ⚠️ Read the FIRST triage comment, not the last one — the scope is already ruled

This card carries two later comments that read like open questions. They are not. **Triage ruled the scope at grading on 2026-08-25T04:03:36Z**, verbatim and ⛔ not re-litigable:

> scope ruled at grading: add a cross-package drift PIN (a test asserting the plugin-security `isHumanUser` agrees with plugin-auth's consolidated `isHumanUserRow` on the shared row corpus), **NOT the consolidation itself** — moving the predicate into `@objectstack/spec`/`platform-objects` expands a published surface, which #11767 rightly refused to carry and which **stays declined here absent new pull** (the contradiction class already bit once; the pin closes that risk without new API). **If the pin proves impractical across the package boundary, stop and report** — the consolidation question then goes to the decision box, not into the PR.

⚠️ The 15:26Z routing note further down the thread lays out an A/B/C fork and asks triage to grade it. **That grading had already happened eleven hours earlier** — the note's author read the card but not the earlier comment. Option **C in that table is the ruled shape**; A and B are the declined ones. I am naming this explicitly because the thread reads backwards: the newest comment on this card is the *stalest* thing on it.

⇒ Deliverable: **the agreement pin**. ⛔ Not the move to `@objectstack/spec/system`. ⛔ Not making `plugin-security` depend on `plugin-auth` in production code.

## Verified on `origin/main` @ `27b6902` — the three spellings are live

| # | site | shape |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `plugin-security/src/bootstrap-platform-admin.ts:401` | `const isHumanUser = (u: any) => u && u.id !== SystemUserId.SYSTEM && u.role !== 'system'` — used at `:426` and `:472` |
| 2 | `plugin-auth/src/audience-posture.ts:317` | `export function isHumanUserRow(row: unknown): boolean` — the #11767 consolidated owner |
| 3 | consumers of (2) | `auth-manager.ts:3653`, `auth-plugin.ts:1706` |

So the population the pin must cover is: whatever rows make (1) and (2) **disagree**. The card names the one that matters — a database still carrying the legacy `usr_system` service row (`SystemUserId.SYSTEM`), present in every DB an older runtime created.

## ⭐ The load-bearing constraint, and the reason this is M and not S

**`plugin-security` does not depend on `plugin-auth`.** That is the whole reason #11767 left the third copy behind, and it is the thing that decides whether this card is buildable:

- A test that imports both packages needs that edge to exist **at least as a dev dependency**, and this repo gates cross-package test inputs — `check:cross-package-test-inputs` is a real family here and it will have an opinion. Run it early, not at the end.
- ⚠️ If a **devDependency** edge is acceptable to the gate and the workspace, that is the cheap route and the pin is straightforward.
- ⚠️ If it is not — if pinning the agreement requires a production dependency edge or a new export — then per the ruling above you **stop and report**. ⛔ Do not add a production dependency to buy a test. Say what you measured and what it would cost; the consolidation question then goes to the decision box.

That fork is the card. Both outcomes are good runs; one of them has a PR and one of them does not.

## ⛔ Explicitly out of scope — named so you do not drift into them

- **A repo-wide census pin** ("find every spelling of this predicate anywhere"). A later comment on the thread raises census-vs-three-site as an open choice. The ruled shape is the **agreement comparison** between the two named owners. A census is a different, larger piece of work — ⭐ if you think it is the better instrument, **file it as its own card** and say why; do not substitute it.
- **Fixing a disagreement you find.** If the two predicates already disagree on some row shape, that is a **finding and possibly a live defect** — report it with the row and both answers. ⛔ Do not "make them agree" by editing one of them; which one is right is not yours (or mine) to decide silently.

## PM mechanism assumptions — falsify them, they are not rulings

- I assume `isHumanUser` (1) and `isHumanUserRow` (2) are **semantically identical today** and the pin will pass on first write. I have compared them by reading, not by executing. If they differ, the card gets more valuable, not less.
- I assume the shared corpus can be expressed as plain row fixtures (no engine, no boot). If the predicates need a live user table to be exercised, say so — that changes the pin's cost.

## Verification

- The pin must be **falsifiable**: per this lane's standing commitment, every negative pin gets **dissolution verification** — break one predicate deliberately, show the pin turn **red**, quote the failure output, restore and verify disk == index == HEAD. ⭐ A pin that has never been seen red is not evidence.
- Derived gate union from `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` on your actual changed set, exit codes captured **before** any pipe. `check:cross-package-test-inputs` in particular.
- **Changeset**: a test-only change ships nothing — argue `skip-changeset` explicitly; ⛔ never an empty changeset.
- ⛔ No model names in any pushed artifact.

## Report

Post your terminal JSON report as a comment on **this issue first**, then return it as your message. Leave **your own** claim comment (your session id + branch) before starting — ⛔ the assignee on this card is the PM session, not you.

I set this card up as a fork: build the pin if a devDependency edge suffices, **stop and report** if it needs a production edge or a new export. The dev did something better than pick a side — it measured that the fork is **asymmetric**:

- `isHumanUserRow` is module-scope-exported but **not reachable from outside `plugin-auth`** — not re-exported from `src/index.ts`, absent from the `exports` map. ⭐ Verified **against the built artifact**: importing `plugin-auth/dist/index.mjs` and reading `isHumanUserRow` yields `undefined`. | claim | reading |
|---|---|
| devDependency only, no production edge | ✓ the one added line sits in **`devDependencies`**, after `plugin-hono-server`; the production `dependencies` block (ending `jose`) is untouched |
